claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories for publishing packages per the strategies in this guide; following them improves reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository.
The version of a source-based Pulumi package is the Git tag on its repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply semver Git tag, run pulumi package publish), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
`pulumi package publish` sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
The Private Registry is part of Pulumi IDP (linked at /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/).
In both source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.
A repository containing multiple Pulumi packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that conflicts with how Pulumi consumes packages.
Pulumi recommends that a repository contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and expected, and ship together at the package's version.
Pulumi recommends defining exactly one package per repository, grouping a cohesive set of components in that package, and using multiple repositories, one per package, for distinct packages.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
The components in the Pulumi EKS package are almost always used together and tend to evolve together.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo with one giant package for all of an organization's components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way regardless of whether each changed, which violates semver.

In the example, releasing the package at v1.1.0 after an enhancement to ComponentA and v2.0.0 after a breaking change to ComponentB follows semver bumping (minor for enhancement, major for breaking change).
A cross-reference to the Publishing packages guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.

Link targets exist: /docs/iac/concepts/packages/, /docs/iac/concepts/components/, packaging-components anchors #source-based-plugin-packages and #executable-based-plugin-packages, /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/.
